#  | Portable Python 3.x Interpreter in Modern C

> pocketpy is a small Python 3.x interpreter written in C11, designed for embedding in games and other C/C++ applications. The core interpreter has no third-party dependencies.

- [pocketpy](https://pocketpy.github.io/index.md): pocketpy
- [Quick start](https://pocketpy.github.io/quick-start.md): Use a C11 compiler and CMake 3.20 or newer. On Windows, use an MSVC environment with C11 atomics support. C++ bindings additionally require C++17.
- [Build configuration](https://pocketpy.github.io/build.md): Quick start covers the default build. This page explains the options that change what the interpreter can do.
- [C Bindings](https://pocketpy.github.io/bindings.md): A binding converts Python arguments to native values, calls your C code, and writes a Python result. All native functions use the py_CFunction signature:
- [C++ Bindings](https://pocketpy.github.io/bindings-cpp.md): pocketpy bundles a C++17 binding layer with a pybind11-style API in include/pybind11/. Use these headers with the pocketpy library. It implements a subset of pybind11 and does not use CPython's extension ABI.
- [Module Reference](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/index.md): pocketpy includes a focused set of Python modules and game-oriented extensions. These pages describe the APIs shipped in this repository, including differences from CPython.
- [Script style](https://pocketpy.github.io/coding-style-guide.md): These conventions keep pocketpy examples readable and make scripts easier to share with Python users. Runtime restrictions belong in the compatibility guide; style preferences do not change language behavior.
- [Performance](https://pocketpy.github.io/performance.md): Measure pocketpy with your application's workload, compiler, target hardware, and enabled features. Results from one script or an older interpreter version do not predict the performance of all Python programs.
- [License](https://pocketpy.github.io/license.md): pkpy is licensed under the MIT License.

## C API

- [C API Essentials](https://pocketpy.github.io/c-api/introduction.md): Include pocketpy.h and initialize the runtime before calling the API. The quick start has a complete host program. Public declarations live in pocketpy.h; the function reference is generated from that header.
- [Execution and Exceptions](https://pocketpy.github.io/c-api/execution.md): API
- [Modules and Host Callbacks](https://pocketpy.github.io/c-api/modules.md): A module holds Python globals. Native modules created with py_newmodule() can be imported by scripts in the current VM, just like source modules.
- [Functions](https://pocketpy.github.io/c-api/functions.md)

## Language and Tools

- [Language Features](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/basic.md): pocketpy supports the core Python constructs used in application scripts. The compatibility guide explains where their behavior differs from CPython; support for a construct does not imply support for every Python variant of it.
- [Comparison with CPython](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/differences.md): pocketpy is designed for embedded scripting. It follows familiar Python syntax while keeping a smaller runtime and library. Test scripts on the same pocketpy build that your application ships.
- [Unsupported Operations](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/ub.md): The following operations violate runtime assumptions. They may crash the interpreter or produce incorrect results instead of a Python exception.
- [Compute Threads](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/threading.md): A pocketpy VM contains independent modules, globals, and Python objects. There are 16 VM slots, indexed 0 through 15; VM 0 is the default. Only one native thread may access a particular VM at a time.
- [Bytecode Deployment](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/deploy.md): pocketpy can compile scripts to .pyc files and run them without the original source. This avoids parsing at load time; it does not make the executed bytecode itself faster.
- [Debugging](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/debugging.md): The pocketpy VS Code extension connects to the interpreter's debug server. Use a build with OS support for the default transport, and keep the Python sources used by that build available.
- [Profiling](https://pocketpy.github.io/features/profiling.md): The line profiler shows where a script spends execution time. Use it to locate expensive lines, then measure performance again without profiling overhead.

## Modules

- [array2d](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/array2d.md): A rectangular grid for tile maps, images, cellular simulations, and other 2D data. Coordinates are column first, row second: grid[x, y].
- [base64](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/base64.md): Convert binary data to and from the standard Base64 alphabet.
- [bisect](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/bisect.md): Find insertion positions in an already sorted list. Searching takes logarithmic time; insertion still moves list elements and can take linear time.
- [cmath](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/cmath.md): Complex-number arithmetic implemented in Python. Construct values with complex(real, imag=0) or imaginary literals such as 2j.
- [collections](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/collections.md): Small container helpers for counting, grouping, and queues.
- [cute_png](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/cute_png.md): PNG decoding and encoding backed by the bundled cute_png library.
- [dataclasses](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/dataclasses.md): @dataclass uses annotated fields to supply __init__, __repr__, __eq__, and __ne__ when the class does not define them.
- [datetime](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/datetime.md): Basic local dates and times, backed by time.localtime().
- [easing](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/easing.md): Convert normalized animation progress into an interpolation weight. Each function takes t and returns a float.
- [enum](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/enum.md): Subclass Enum to give constants readable names and values.
- [functools](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/functools.md): Helpers for caching calls, reducing a sequence, and pre-filling arguments.
- [gc](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/gc.md): Control the current VM's tracing garbage collector.
- [heapq](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/heapq.md): Use a list as a min-heap: heap[0] is the smallest item, while the rest of the list is not necessarily sorted.
- [importlib](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/importlib.md): reload(module) re-executes an already imported source module and returns the same module object. It reloads .py source through the current VM's import callback, not compiled .pyc or native modules.
- [inspect and dis](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/inspection.md): Inspect function metadata and the bytecode that pocketpy executes.
- [json](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/json.md): Serialize simple data as JSON text.
- [lz4](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/lz4.md): Fast compression of byte strings.
- [math](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/math.md): Real-number functions and constants. Most functions accept an int or float and return a float; exceptions are noted below. Arguments to native functions are positional.
- [msgpack](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/msgpack.md): Encode simple values in the MessagePack binary format.
- [operator](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/operator.md): Function forms of Python operators, useful for callbacks and reductions.
- [os and io](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/os.md): Host filesystem access, available when PK_ENABLE_OS=1.
- [periphery](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/periphery.md): Low-level bindings to the bundled c-periphery library for Linux GPIO, SPI, I2C, serial, PWM, LED, and memory-mapped I/O.
- [pickle](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/pickle.md): Save Python object graphs as bytes and restore them within pocketpy.
- [picoterm and conio](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/console.md): Terminal helpers for text-based interfaces.
- [pkpy](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/pkpy.md): pocketpy-specific runtime controls and diagnostics.
- [random](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/random.md): Pseudo-random numbers from a Mersenne Twister generator. Module-level functions use a shared generator in the current VM; Random creates independent state. This generator is for simulations and games, not cryptographic secrets.
- [stdc](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/stdc.md): Typed native storage and raw-memory operations for C bindings.
- [sys](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/sys.md): Interpreter identification, host-supplied arguments, and recursion limits.
- [time](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/time.md): Clock access and a small local-time interface.
- [traceback](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/traceback.md): Report the exception currently being handled by a Python except block.
- [typing](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/typing.md): A compatibility module for annotations and static-analysis tools. It does not enforce types at runtime.
- [unicodedata](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/unicodedata.md): This module provides east_asian_width(character), returning the Unicode East Asian width classification of one character.
- [vmath](https://pocketpy.github.io/modules/vmath.md): Native vector, matrix, and color types for game scripts.
